enAudit: G2-311 (Two Sentences: Full Stop or Question Mark?) — the instruction asserts something the page contradicts. 'Two sentences ran together, and one of them is a question.' On g2311-fruits.png card 3 the item is 'the fig is next to the box max draws two figs for leo': NEITHER half is a question. A child obeying the instruction inserts a question mark where none belongs, and the title reinforces it. Either the generator must guarantee one interrogative per item, or the instruction must be permissive ('choose the right end mark for each'). We wrote the Norwegian permissively for this reason.

G1-302 (Unscramble the Sentence: Find the Beginning) — the ungated animacy frame is still live. g1302-fruits.png card 1 is 'feeds / the / avocado. / leo' -> 'Leo feeds the avocado.' You cannot feed an avocado. This is the recorded 'tom feeds the skateboard' class from the nt20-B-VAR EN sweep, unfixed: the 'feeds' frame is still being applied to an inanimate/fruit noun. Every locale inherits the frame verbatim.

G1-293 and G1-300 (word-classes, 2-bin) — the copy names controls the page does not have. The title and instruction say 'naming word' / 'doing word' / 'describing word', but the bins on the very same sheet are labelled 'Nouns' / 'Verbs' and 'Nouns' / 'Adjectives'. The child is told to sort into two things that appear nowhere. The formal term is the correct one (it is what the sibling G2-275 already ships, and what the Norwegian page renders: Substantiv / Verb / Adjektiv), so the TITLE and INSTRUCTION should move to it, not the bin labels.

G1-300 — the instruction is generic and does not distinguish the page. 'Sort each word into the right bin.' is equally true of G1-293, G2-285, G2-286, G2-287 and the base G2-275. What is actually different here (adjectives rather than verbs; the chips carry no picture support, unlike G1-293) is never stated.

Three instructions are statements, not tasks, and never tell the child to do anything. G1-304: 'The word bank, the letter boxes and the first letter are all there to help.' never says WRITE THE WORD. G2-311: 'Two sentences ran together, and one of them is a question.' never says rewrite them (its sibling G2-307 does). G1-294: 'Every dot is numbered here, and the whole way is backwards.' never says JOIN THE DOTS — and it is a K/G1 page.

G1-301, G1-303, G1-304 (write-the-word) — the instruction describes only half of each card. Every card carries TWO write surfaces: a ruled handwriting line AND a row of letter boxes. G1-301 says only 'Write one letter in each box' and never mentions the line; G1-304 mentions the boxes but not the line. A teacher cannot tell whether the child writes the word twice or once.

G2-312 (How Many Days Later?) — the title over-promises. Only 1 of the 4 questions on g2312-nothm.png is a 'how many days after' question; the other three are a sticker-date lookup, a one-week-later date, and a day-of-the-week. The title names the minority case. (We retitled the Norwegian to cover the actual mix.)

G2-296 / G2-297 / G2-312 (calendar) — the month grid starts the week on SUNDAY. That is a US convention. Norway, and de/nl/sv/da/fi and the Romance locales, start the week on MONDAY, and Norwegian classroom calendars additionally carry a week-number column. A Sunday-leading grid is immediately wrong to a Norwegian teacher, and the 'one week later' / 'how many Mondays' questions are read off a layout no Norwegian classroom uses. Same artefact class as the US cents: note the currency table itself IS correct for no (NOK, kr, coins 1/5/10/20), so only the week-start is outstanding.

K-315 (Copy the Capitals) — the title names letters, the page holds words. 'Look at the capitals, then write them yourself' reads as a capital-letter alphabet drill; k315-toys.png shows whole words (DICE, CRAYONS, BICYCLE) set in capitals with two writing rows. The task is copying a WORD written in capitals, not copying capitals.

G1-298 / G1-299 ('Just the Numbers') — an unexplained empty frame on every card. The no-pictures variant still renders the picture band as an empty white dotted panel above each equation (g1298-fruits.png, g1299-animals.png). Neither title nor instruction mentions it, and to a 6-year-old an empty framed box reads as somewhere to draw. Suppress the band, or say what it is for.

G1-296 / G1-297 — the picture rows overflow the card and are clipped mid-image. g1296-vehicles.png cards 1, 4 and 5 and g1297-toys.png card 3 run past both card edges, so on a page whose entire task is COUNTING the group the child cannot see the whole group. Language-independent; it will ship in all 11 locales.
G1-286 (Doubles and Halves with Pictures to 20) — 'to 20' but the largest value on the page is 18, and it carries 4 cards where every sibling in the family carries 6 or 8.

out/b2var-faces.json — the `sweep` path is WRONG for all 36 new faces, and `sweepExists` is false for every one of them. It names g1298-nothm.png where the file is g1298-fruits.png, and g1292-toys.png where the file is g1292-toys-pt.png. A panel that trusted the flag would conclude the 36 new pages had never been rendered and would write them blind — which is exactly the failure the brief warns about. All 36 ARE rendered and we read every one.

G1-292 — the only render that exists is a Portuguese probe carrying English chrome (g1292-toys-pt.png: Portuguese word chips and o/a bins under an English title and instruction). The article bins are the one thing about this face a panel must see in its own language, and there is no en render at all. Separately, the English instruction 'Read every word. Write it under the word that belongs in front of it.' never names the article, and 'the word that belongs in front of it' is a hard parse for a 6-year-old.

G2-297 — its sweep render is stale. g2297-nothm.png shows 'This month is full. Read the calendar carefully to answer every question.' while strings.en.json and the faces table both carry 'Find the date one week later, and count the days between the stickers.' The current English also names only 2 of the 5 question types the page actually asks.
